bib.title: ChartQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering about Charts with Visual and Logical Reasoning
bib.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2022, pages 2263-2279

question: Can models answer human-written visual and logical reasoning questions about real-world charts, and how well do table-QA and vision-language models do when the chart's data table is extracted from the image?
hypothesis: Combining visual features with an extracted data table, and training on human-written questions, handles visual and compositional chart questions better than fixed-vocabulary classification or table-only approaches; the new dataset is harder than earlier ones.
contributions: A large-scale ChartQA dataset with real-world charts and human-authored question-answer pairs
A pipeline approach that combines visual features and automatically extracted data from charts in transformer-based QA models
An extensive analysis and evaluation of the performance of the models

method.summary: Benchmark of 4,804 charts / 9,608 human-written questions (ChartQA-H) plus 17,141 charts / 23,111 T5-generated questions from Statista summaries (ChartQA-M). Pipeline: extend ChartOCR (plus CRAFT text recognition) to extract a structured data table from the chart image, then feed table, question and optionally image features to T5, VL-T5, TaPas or the new VisionTaPas (ViT + TaPas + 4-layer cross-modality encoder).
method.task: chart question answering (open-vocabulary, numeric and label answers)

datasets.name: ChartQA-H
datasets.source: AMT annotators on charts from Statista (2,484), Pew (1,303), OWID (786), OECD (231)
datasets.preprocessing: Pew has no underlying tables; two questions per chart (compositional and visual); second annotator answers, disagreements manually resolved

datasets.name: ChartQA-M
datasets.source: T5 answer-extraction and answer-aware question-generation models fine-tuned on SQuAD, applied to Statista human-written summaries
datasets.preprocessing: filtered out questions whose answer is not in the chart data table; test set manually cleaned of invalid questions; 86.64% of 1,250 inspected pairs valid

datasets.name: PlotQA
datasets.split: Test V1, V2; also pretraining for ChartQA

models.name: VisionTaPas
models.params: inferred: roughly TaPas-base + ViT-base + cross-modal layers (total not stated)
models.architecture: ViT encoder + TaPas encoder + 4-block cross-modality encoder; aggregation head extended with difference, ratio and fixed-vocabulary classes
models.init_from: ViT pretrained weights (Dosovitskiy 2021); TaPas weights pretrained on WikiTQ

other.visual_input: Mask R-CNN (ResNet-101, detectron2, COCO init) mark features, zero-padded to 36

models.name: PReFIL
models.architecture: classification, parallel fusion of question and image

models.name: ChartOCR extension
models.architecture: CornerNet-style keypoint detectors + CRAFT OCR + color/position heuristics

training.objective: T5/VL-T5: generate answer text; TaPas/VisionTaPas: aggregation and cell-selection heads, difference/ratio trained with heuristic (24% noisy) cell supervision
training.lr: VisionTaPas 1e-5 (0.00001); T5 and VL-T5 1e-4 (0.0001); TaPas FigureQA 1e-5; PReFIL 1e-3; Mask R-CNN 0.00025
training.batch_size: VisionTaPas 64; T5 40; VL-T5 96; TaPas 24 (48 FigureQA); PReFIL 128; PlotQA* 1; Mask R-CNN 8
training.epochs: On ChartQA: VisionTaPas 30, T5 30, VL-T5 30, PlotQA* 20; VisionTaPas 4 (FigureQA, DVQA), 1 (PlotQA); T5 4 (FigureQA/DVQA/PlotQA); VL-T5 20 (FigureQA/DVQA), 10 (PlotQA); PReFIL 100
training.hardware: one 4-V100 GPU machine and one 4-A100 GPU machine
training.compute: longest run VL-T5 on PlotQA, about 64-70 hours on 4 V100

other.pretraining_transfer: VisionTaPas and VL-T5 pretrained on PlotQA then fine-tuned on ChartQA

inference.decoding: T5 beam search size 4; VL-T5 beam search size 5
inference.samples: single run per model, no seeds or variance reported

metrics.name: Relaxed accuracy
metrics.definition: numeric answers correct if within 5% of gold; non-numeric need exact match

metrics.name: Data extraction score
metrics.definition: 1/L sum over charts of 1 - cost/K, with D(gt,pr)=min(1,|gt-pr|/gt) and linear-sum assignment matching of values

eval.protocol: Two settings: gold data table provided or extracted by ChartOCR; per-subset, per-chart-type and 200-question per-type breakdown; no seeds or significance tests.

evidence.quote: We consider an answer to be correct if it is within 5% of the gold answer.

limits: Models cannot handle nested operations (add then subtract); VisionTaPas has only single difference and ratio ops.
Data table and visual features are combined separately, so chart structure is not fully captured.
Pipeline is modular and error-prone: 83.85% extraction accuracy on ChartQA and a 16 point drop vs gold tables; extraction metric ignores textual tokens.
Only bar, line and pie charts; logarithmic-scale charts unsupported by ChartOCR.
Pew charts have no gold tables so data extraction cannot be scored there.
No seeds, variance or significance tests; single run per model.
Authors note the models could be abused to mislead about chart content.
Dated: pipeline (extract table then table-QA) predates end-to-end multimodal LLMs; numbers are 2022 baselines.
Inconsistency: text says 79.4% of bar charts simple and 29.6% complex (sums to 109%).

terms.definition: questions that contain at least two mathematical/logical operations like sum, difference and average
questions that refer to the visual attributes such as color, height, and length of graphical marks
